I have what I need from source, and I deliberately did **not** read the four panel members' substantive answers before forming my own — the method demands an independent verdict, and reading theirs first would contaminate it. (Note: `cc2.json` is 96 bytes — the CC2 panelist returned empty; the live panel is 4/5, not 5/5.)

Here is my independent, source-grounded contribution. Every load-bearing claim below was checked against the repository, not the brief text.

---

## Q1 — TOPOLOGY

**Four per-domain modules, one domain config per run, run as a single batched launcher pass.**

This is forced, not preferred. Verified in `reference_runner_v2.py`: the runner loads exactly one `cfg.domain`, and `dm_config.domain = cfg.domain` propagates that single domain into the immune pipeline; `_specialist_b_cell_dispatch(triaged, domain_config)` then reads only *that* one TOML's `verification_tools`. A consolidated multi-domain module run under one config would route every claim through one domain's patterns — a SMILES claim in a `mathematics`-configured run never reaches `chemistry_structure` (RDKit) at all. The `cross_domain.toml` escape isn't in the live set and its routes omit `stoichiometric_balance`, `linear_programming`, and `astronomical` — precisely the three tools Rounds 3 added. So consolidation forgoes exactly the coverage the correction rounds bought.

**What four per-domain modules measure:** per-domain ground-truthed recall of planted-false claims with each domain's *full* routing table live, plus per-domain discriminative capacity (confirm true claims, reject planted ones), scorable against each module's answer key.

**What it forgoes:** cross-domain interaction defects — a claim false only because of a chemistry→engineering boundary. The single-domain runner architecturally cannot route such a claim, so it cannot test it. That gap is out of scope for the specialist-validation purpose (per-domain noise filtering) and closing it is a separate work item (build `cross_domain.toml` into the live set with the three missing tools), not a synth-module topology choice.

**Cost:** ~4 × \$6–20 = \$24–80 vs ~\$6–20 for one consolidated run. The saving is real but buys nothing measurable — the audit already established the 1-module case now rests only on cost, and cost alone doesn't justify surrendering 3/4 of the domains' routing coverage.

## Q2 — COVERAGE GAPS

Verified against §2a + TOMLs. Chemistry §2a clusters: SMILES / stoichiometry / mol-weight / functional-group + one planted-false — **no logical, no statistical** cluster, yet `chemistry.toml` routes logical → `[z3, sympy]` and statistical → `[statsmodels, scipy, uncertainty_propagation]`. Engineering §2a: load-factor / material-tolerance / safety-factor / dimensional / LP + planted-false — **no logical** cluster, yet routes logical → `[z3]`. (Sub-gap: engineering's material-tolerance cluster exercises `scipy` + `uncertainties` but never `statsmodels`; a Weibull/reliability claim would close it — noted, not the primary gap.)

**Cap management** (mirrors how physics/biology kept to the 4–6 limit): I fold the planted-false *into* the new clusters rather than adding a standalone planted cluster, so each module lands at exactly 6.

**Design note that applies to both** — the planted claim's *wording* must trigger the domain's `claim_patterns` regex or it silently routes to the wrong verifier. Example: `chemistry.toml`'s logical pattern is `(?:exothermic.*\bincrease\b)`; a claim phrased "shifts toward products" won't match, but "an exothermic reaction's product yield will **increase** at higher temperature" will. The brief must verify each example against the TOML regex — the same class of check Rounds 2–3 performed.

**Chemistry — new clusters:**

- **Equilibrium-shift & conservation logic** (route: `z3` satisfiability + `sympy` sign-check). Le Chatelier direction claims and mass/charge-conservation booleans. `chemistry.toml` logical patterns already name Le Chatelier and exothermic/endothermic. *Planted false (embedded here):* "an exothermic reaction's product yield will **increase** at higher temperature" — contradicts Le Chatelier; z3 encodes the sign rule and returns unsat; the specialist rejects.
- **Analytical-measurement statistics** (route: `statsmodels` / `scipy` / `uncertainty_propagation`). Beer–Lambert calibration regression (R², slope with CI), and molarity uncertainty propagated from mass ± δm, volume ± δV. *Planted false (embedded here):* a stated R² = 0.99 that scipy recomputes as ~0.7 from the given points, or a propagated σ_M inconsistent with the component uncertainties.

Chemistry becomes {SMILES, stoichiometry(retains original unbalanced-eqn planted), mol-weight, functional-group, logical(+planted), statistical(+planted)} = 6.

**Engineering — new cluster:**

- **Failure-mode & load-path logic** (route: `z3`). Fault-tree / redundancy / load-path-conservation booleans; `engineering.toml` logical patterns name FMEA, fault-tree, conservation-violation. Examples: "structure survives iff ≥2 of 3 redundant members carry load; A and B have failed, therefore it survives" (z3 unsat — only 1 remains); the "dissipation asserted negative" energy-balance contradiction (same shape as physics cluster 5). *Planted false (embedded here):* the 2-of-3 redundancy claim above, asserted to survive when the boolean model shows failure.

Engineering becomes {load-factor, material-tolerance, safety-factor, dimensional, LP, logical(+planted)} = 6 (the original LP-constraint-violation planted moves inside LP, keeping ≥1).

## Q3 — EARN-THEIR-KEEP METRIC

A conjunctive gate — one-sided metrics validate only one failure mode. Measured per domain against each synth module's answer key. **Instrumentation prerequisite:** every `CellVerdict` must log `{classified-type, routed-tool, verdict, ground-truth}`, or the metric can't distinguish a mis-routed planted claim (module defect) from a route that failed to catch (specialist defect).

1. **Attributed planted-false recall = 1.0.** Every planted false is rejected **and** the rejecting verdict is attributed to the domain-routed specialist tool (`chemistry_structure`, `linear_programming`, …), *not* the general cell. Exact threshold, not statistical: with ~6 planted claims each within its routed tool's competence, any miss is a named broken route — fix it, don't average it. The attribution clause is the actual "earn their keep": a planted false caught by the baseline sympy/z3 cell earns the *specialist* nothing.
2. **Zero specialist false positives on true claims.** No known-true module claim is rejected by a specialist verdict. Threshold 0, not ε — every such reject is a broken route injecting noise into the filter whose entire purpose is removing it.
3. **≥1 attributed decision-change per domain**, measured by a paired specialist-on vs specialist-off run on the same seed/module. If dispositions are identical everywhere, the layer is inert — it earns nothing even at recall 1.0, because the baseline already caught everything. This is the counterfactual the K/L/M non-distortion gate never had data for.
4. **γ non-distortion on an all-true control module.** Specialist-on and specialist-off must reach the same convergence round and the same γ trajectory (within logging precision) on a module with no planted falses. Protects the load-bearing decay curve — the layer must move outcomes only through legitimate attributed catches.

VALIDATED = (1) ∧ (2) ∧ (3) ∧ (4), per domain, across the four modules.

**What falsifies "specialists earn their keep":** planted falses caught only by the general cell (attribution fails); identical on/off dispositions (decision-changed = 0, inert layer); any specialist reject on a known-true claim (FP > 0, worse than nothing); or any γ/round shift on the all-true control (distorts the governing measure).

## Q4 — NON-CODE FINDING SCHEMA

Decisive source fact: `reverify_falsifier` runs the falsifier as a **subprocess with the repo on PYTHONPATH, 30 s timeout**, verdict from `AssertionError`/`FALSIFIED`. This mechanism is **domain-agnostic** — a falsifier importing `sympy`/`rdkit`/`pulp`/`z3` re-runs identically to one importing a repo module. The only code-specific coupling is the directive text "import the REAL target module" + file:line citation. So the bridge is small.

**Schema (claim + evidence + falsifier):**

- **Claim** — one falsifiable assertion lifted from the solution.
- **Artefact citation** (replaces file:line) — the exact solution step/part number **plus the verbatim quote** of the artefact the claim rests on (the sequence, the equation, the numbers). The code rule "don't retype the function, import the real one" becomes "**transcribe the solution artefact verbatim; do not idealise it**" — the falsifier must test what the solution *actually* produced.
- **Evidence** — the routed tool's output on that artefact ("tool output IS the evidence").
- **Falsifier** (runnable, runner-re-executed) — a Python block that encodes the solution's artefact verbatim, imports the real verification library, and raises/`FALSIFIED` iff the property is genuinely false, exits clean iff true.

Concrete runnable falsifiers:
- **Construction step (FT-001):** transcribe the solution's exact 16 numbers, compute LIS/LDS, `assert LIS < 5` — raises iff the solution's own sequence contains a length-5 monotone subsequence.
- **Stoichiometric balance:** parse the solution's exact equation string, atom-count both sides via `stoichiometric_balance`/RDKit, `assert not balanced` raises iff genuinely unbalanced.
- **Buckling calc:** transcribe stated E, I, K, L and claimed P_cr, recompute `π²EI/(KL)²` with `sympy` + `pint` (dimensional check folded in), assert relative error < tol.
- **Deductive proof step with no computable object** (e.g. "no two elements share the same label pair"): **not universally mechanically falsifiable.** Either encode the specific finite instance the step relies on in z3/sympy and check entailment, or mark it **UNTOOLABLE → HIL** — reusing the existing critical-with-no-falsifier routing rather than fabricating a fake falsifier. The honest boundary: each solution-claim must be *partitioned* into mechanically-falsifiable sub-claims (get runnable falsifiers) and deductive-validity sub-claims (UNTOOLABLE→HIL, or LLM specialist verdict capped at 0.5 per the DeepSeek formal-verification cap already on record).

**Specialist-dispatch role when the artefact is a solution:** `_specialist_b_cell_dispatch` already operates on triaged *claims*, not on file:line, so it works unchanged. Its role shifts from "noise filter over a module's claims" to "**the router that classifies the solution's claim and decides which tool the falsifier is built around**." Specialist = router (which tool); runnable falsifier = the executable (that tool run, re-runnable by the runner). Two views of one "tools decide." The CONFIRM-only-for-criticals asymmetry carries over intact: a REFUTED critical isn't trusted to clear (a broken falsifier clean-exits and masks a real defect), so a critical solution-defect clears only by active demonstration or HIL. **Net: C2 is a claim-extraction + falsifier-authoring layer on top of an unchanged verification core.**

## Q5 — FACTORIAL TARGET

**A fresh synthesised module with a known answer key (single domain, richest routing — mathematics or physics), NOT the runner-tests-runner self-test.**

The 2×2 measures whether feedback and divergence change finding quality/coverage — which requires **ground truth** to score. The synth module has an answer key (planted falses + known-true claims); runner-tests-runner does not (its own bugs are unknown-unknowns — the reason to test it, but the reason it's a bad *factorial substrate*: you can't score four cells against truth, so "feedback improved findings" becomes unfalsifiable). Frozen thresholds also favour fixed module content over the actively-changing runner code, and reusing an already-converged module gives the (off,off) baseline cell a known-good reference to reproduce — protecting baseline-cell integrity. For the divergence directive specifically, only a module with planted defects lets `_divergence.py`'s isomorphism check score whether the divergent alternative found a *second real defect* vs cosmetic rewording.

## Independent self-falsification (per the method)

**Q1-POSITION:** Four per-domain modules, one domain config each, batched into a single launcher pass — forced by one-domain-per-run + the `cross_domain.toml` coverage gap; measures per-domain answer-keyed recall + discrimination; forgoes cross-domain interaction defects (out of scope, needs cross_domain built).
**Q1-FALSIFICATION:** If the goal is validating the *dispatch mechanism* rather than each domain's content, one richly-routed domain arguably validates the parameterised function and the other three are cost with no mechanism-level information. Rebuttal: the failure modes are per-TOML (the very Q2 logical/statistical gaps), invisible unless each domain's actual routing table is exercised against its own key — so the cost buys per-TOML validation, the real risk surface. Concession: under a hard budget cap, run chemistry and engineering first — their TOMLs changed most and are least validated.

**Q2-CLUSTERS (chemistry):** add *Equilibrium-shift & conservation logic* (z3 + sympy; planted: exothermic-yield-increases-with-heat) and *Analytical-measurement statistics* (statsmodels/scipy/uncertainties; planted: unsupported R² or propagated σ) → 6 clusters, planted folded in.
**Q2-CLUSTERS (engineering):** add *Failure-mode & load-path logic* (z3; planted: 2-of-3 redundancy asserted to survive with 2 failed) → 6 clusters; statsmodels sub-gap (Weibull/reliability) flagged separately. Every planted claim's wording must be regex-verified against the TOML `claim_patterns` or it mis-routes.

**Q3-CRITERIA (with thresholds):** conjunctive gate per domain — (1) attributed planted-false recall = 1.0 (caught by the routed specialist, not the baseline); (2) specialist false-positive rate = 0 on known-true claims; (3) ≥1 attributed decision-change per domain vs a specialist-off paired run; (4) identical convergence round + γ trajectory on an all-true control. Prerequisite: per-verdict logging of {classified-type, routed-tool, verdict, ground-truth}.
**Q3-FALSIFICATION:** strict 1.0/0 thresholds conflate module-authoring defects (mis-worded planted claim routes wrong) with specialist defects — brittle unless the instrumentation distinguishes them; the required per-claim logging is what makes the gate diagnostic rather than a blunt pass/fail, and I'm treating that logging as part of the criteria, not optional.

**Q4-SCHEMA:** claim + verbatim artefact citation (replaces file:line) + tool-output evidence + runnable falsifier that transcribes the solution's artefact verbatim, imports the real library, raises/`FALSIFIED` iff the property is genuinely false. Partition each claim into mechanically-falsifiable (runnable falsifier) vs deductive-only (UNTOOLABLE→HIL or 0.5-capped LLM verdict). The subprocess re-execution core, CONFIRM-only asymmetry, and HIL routing are all reused unchanged.
**Q4-SPECIALIST-ROLE:** the dispatch operates on claims, not file:line, so it's unchanged — it becomes the router that classifies the solution's claim and selects the tool the falsifier is built around; specialist = which-tool, falsifier = the-tool-run. C2 is a claim-extraction + falsifier-authoring layer over an unchanged verification core.

**Q5-POSITION:** a fresh answer-keyed synth module (single domain, richest routing), not runner-tests-runner — because scoring a 2×2 against truth needs a ground-truth substrate and a frozen, already-baselined target.
**Q5-OBJECTION:** a synth module has a small, *designed* defect set, so both feedback-on and feedback-off may hit recall 1.0 fast — a ceiling effect that masks any real feedback/divergence benefit and wrongly reads as "no effect," when the mechanism is exactly meant to help on the deep unknown-bug space that runner-tests-runner resembles. Mitigation (not refutation): a factorial-grade module deliberately over-loaded with 10–15 defects spanning easy→subtle preserves scorability while restoring headroom; the residual — a hand-planted set can't replicate the unknown-unknown structure where feedback most plausibly helps — is the honest cost of choosing scorability over realism.
